concept_options.title: Epic Build — Momentum Across America
concept_options.hook: The road doesn't stop, and neither does the music.
concept_options.visual_approach: Fast, propulsive cutting through the whole 7-week trip; correction-then-grade teal/orange-leaning color; letterbox (2.35:1) reserved for landmark reveal moments only; driving orchestral-hybrid track as the pacing spine with deliberate breaks from the beat grid at scenic payoffs.
key_points: Chronological momentum from departure to return carries the whole edit
Fast cuts through transit/landscape footage, slow holds at hero landmark moments
Music-led pacing with intentional off-beat breaks at emotional peaks
concept_options.core_message: A 7-week US road trip compressed into one continuous, propulsive cinematic arc.
grounded_in: Sam Kolder / Jay Alvarrez style cinematic travel videos
data_point: color correction then creative grade
concept_options.why_this_works: This is the dominant genre convention research surfaced for 'cinematic + epic' travel montages, and directly matches the user's stated mood (cinematic & epic) and platform (YouTube).

concept_options.title: Quiet Wonder — Contemplative Vista
concept_options.hook: Some places don't need a cut. They need a breath.
concept_options.visual_approach: Slower holds, wide vistas given room to breathe, restrained desaturated-warm grade, sparse strings building to one swell near the end; minimal beat-locked cutting.
key_points: Patience over speed — earns 'epic' through scale and stillness rather than pace
One deliberate emotional swell near the close rather than sustained energy throughout
Directly counters mechanical beat-cutting saturation found in research
concept_options.core_message: The trip as a series of moments worth sitting with.
grounded_in: data_point: travel edits vary pace, slow down at payoff moments
underserved_gaps: chronologically messy archive needs emotional throughline
concept_options.why_this_works: Offers a genuinely different emotional register (stillness vs. speed) while staying inside the 'epic' territory the user asked for.

concept_options.title: Chapters Across America — Journey Structure
concept_options.hook: Every stop was its own small story. Together, they're one big one.
concept_options.visual_approach: Clips grouped by date/location into named chapters with title cards per stop; epic build threads through all chapters toward a payoff on the final return-home shot.
key_points: Chaptered structure matches the trip's actual multi-stop, multi-week reality
Title cards per location give the chronologically messy archive a clear spine
Overall arc still builds to an epic payoff at the end
concept_options.core_message: A cross-country journey told as a sequence of chapters that add up to one story.
grounded_in: How To END A Travel Video (3 Tricks)
concept_options.why_this_works: Directly addresses the gap in existing 'cinematic travel video' content, which is mostly built for single-destination shoots, not a 7-week multi-stop archive.

selected_concept.rationale: User selected 'Epic Build' directly — fast, propulsive, music-led momentum edit.

options_considered.rejected_because: User wants one highlight reel, not multiple derivative clips.

options_considered.label: Epic Build — Momentum Across America
options_considered.reason: Matches genre-standard 'epic cinematic travel' convention and user's stated mood directly.

options_considered.label: Quiet Wonder — Contemplative Vista

decisions.subject: Composition runtime for the cinematic edit

options_considered.label: Remotion
options_considered.reason: Video-led composition with <OffthreadVideo>, color-grade overlays, letterbox and title-card support over real source footage — matches this brief's video-led delivery promise.

options_considered.label: HyperFrames
options_considered.reason: Strong for HTML/GSAP kinetic typography and launch-reel style motion.
options_considered.rejected_because: Not built around grading/compositing real source video as the primary layer, which is the core of this brief.

options_considered.label: FFmpeg only
options_considered.rejected_because: Would not support color-grade overlays, letterbox reveal treatment, or title cards needed for the epic-cinematic treatment.

decisions.reason: Both Remotion and HyperFrames were presented per the governance HARD RULE; user explicitly approved Remotion given the video-led nature of the piece.

decisions.subject: Target runtime vs. documented YouTube retention drop-off at 2-3 minutes

options_considered.label: Keep 2-3 minutes
options_considered.reason: Trip spans 7 weeks/multiple stops — more room needed to cover it than under-2-minute format allows.

options_considered.label: Tighten to under 2 minutes
options_considered.reason: Best documented retention, but forces cutting most of the trip's stops.

options_considered.label: Extend to 6-8 minutes
options_considered.reason: Better retention than 2-3min middle ground and more room to tell the story, but longer edit effort.

decisions.reason: Retention data point was surfaced explicitly to the user; user chose to keep the original 2-3 minute target given the trip's length and scope.
